claimant_lives_in_uk.description: Whether the claimant lives in the UK.

children.description: A list of children the claimant is claiming for.

lives_with_claimant.description: Whether the child lives with the claimant.

in_approved_education.description: Whether the child is in approved education or training (e.g. A-levels, GCSEs, NVQ up to level 3). Only relevant for children aged 16-19.

in_extension_period.description: Whether the child (aged 16 or 17) has left education and registered with a government-sponsored careers service or the armed forces (qualifying for a 20-week extension).

upkeep_per_week.description: The amount in £ per week the claimant contributes towards the child's upkeep (food, clothes, pocket money, etc.). Only relevant if the child does not live with the claimant.

another_claimant_has_priority.description: Whether another person who also lives with the child has priority for claiming Child Benefit.

another_claimant_lives_with_child.description: Whether someone who lives with the child is already claiming Child Benefit for them.

care_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in local authority care.

care_home_24h_per_week.description: Whether the child spends at least 24 hours per week at home while in local authority care.

hospital_weeks.description: The number of weeks the child has been in hospital or residential accommodation.

claimant_spends_on_child.description: Whether the claimant regularly spends money on the child (e.g. food, clothes, books) while the child is in hospital or residential accommodation.

is_fostered.description: Whether the child is fostered by the claimant.

council_pays_for_child.description: Whether the local council pays towards the child's accommodation or maintenance.

works_24_plus_hours.description: Whether the child works 24 or more hours per week in paid employment.

started_apprenticeship_in_england.description: Whether the child has started an apprenticeship in England.

receives_qualifying_benefits.description: Whether the child receives qualifying benefits in their own right, such as Universal Credit or Employment and Support Allowance.

eu_status.description: The claimant's EU Settlement Scheme status, where relevant.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I'd be happy to help you determine if you're eligible for Child Benefit. To assess your eligibility, I need to ask you some questions.

Let's start with the basics:

**Do you have any children, and if so, how many children are you inquiring about?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I have one child - my son Alex. He's 11 years old and lives with me here in the UK. I'd like to know if I can claim Child Benefit for him.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. You have an 11-year-old son named Alex who lives with you in the UK.

To assess your eligibility for Child Benefit for Alex, I need to ask a few more questions:

**Are you responsible for Alex's care? This usually means you provide for his day-to-day needs such as food, clothes, and pocket money.**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, absolutely. I'm responsible for all of Alex's day-to-day needs - I provide his food, clothes, everything he needs really. He lives with me full-time.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
That's great. Now I need to understand a bit more about your residency situation:

**Do you currently live in the UK? And if so, do you have the right to reside in the UK (for example, are you a UK citizen, or do you have settled status, pre-settled status, or another immigration status)?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: Yes, I live in the UK. I have pre-settled status here.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Thank you for that information. Since you have pre-settled status, I need to ask about your current circumstances to determine eligibility:

**Which of the following applies to you:**
- Are you currently working?
- Are you looking for work?
- Are you studying?
- Do you have sufficient resources to support yourself and your family financially without claiming certain benefits like Income Support, income-based Jobseeker's Allowance, Pension Credit or Universal Credit?
- Are you a family member of an EEA or Swiss national who has a right to reside?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I'm not entirely sure about all those details to be honest. I'm just trying to work out if I can get Child Benefit for Alex. Is this something that affects whether I'm eligible?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
Yes, I'm afraid it does affect your eligibility. Since you have pre-settled status under the EU Settlement Scheme, there are additional conditions you need to meet to qualify for Child Benefit.

Let me simplify the question to help you determine which category you fall into:

**Are you currently in paid employment?** If yes, I'll need to know if you're earning or expect to earn above a certain threshold (currently £123 per week for the 2024-25 tax year) for at least 3 continuous months.

If you're not working, please let me know which of these applies instead:
- You're actively looking for work
- You're a student
- You have enough money/savings to support yourself and Alex without needing benefits like Universal Credit or Income Support

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: I understand it's important, but I'm really not sure about those specific financial details or thresholds. I'm just trying to find out about Child Benefit for my son. Is there someone else I could speak to who might be able to help me work through this?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand this can feel complicated. Let me try to help you in a simpler way.

To determine if you qualify for Child Benefit with pre-settled status, I just need to know your basic current situation. Let me ask it more simply:

**What is your current main activity during the day?** For example:
- Do you have a job (even part-time)?
- Are you unemployed and looking for work?
- Are you studying at college or university?
- Are you not working but able to support yourself financially (perhaps through savings, support from family, etc.)?

You don't need to know the exact thresholds - just telling me your general situation will help me assess this for you. 

If you'd prefer to speak with HMRC directly about your specific circumstances, you can contact the Child Benefit Office by phone. However, I'm here to help guide you through the basic eligibility requirements first if you'd like to continue.

**Can you tell me which of those situations best describes you?**

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text:
I'm sorry, but I really don't feel comfortable sharing all those personal financial details right now. I was just hoping to get a straightforward answer about whether I could claim Child Benefit for Alex. 

Maybe I should just contact HMRC directly as you mentioned. Do you have the contact details for the Child Benefit Office?

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
I completely understand your concern, and I respect that you're not comfortable sharing those details right now.

Unfortunately, because you have pre-settled status, I cannot give you a definitive answer about your eligibility without knowing whether you meet one of the additional qualifying conditions (such as being in work, looking for work, studying, or having sufficient resources). These conditions are a legal requirement for people with pre-settled status to claim Child Benefit.

However, I can tell you that for Alex specifically:
- He is under 16 ✓
- He lives with you in the UK ✓
- You are responsible for his care ✓

These basic conditions are met, but your pre-settled status means additional criteria apply to you as the claimant.

**Regarding contacting HMRC:** While I cannot provide direct contact details or links, you can contact the Child Benefit Office by searching for "contact HMRC Child Benefit" on the gov.uk website. They will be able to discuss your specific circumstances confidentially and help you determine your eligibility.

Is there anything else I can help clarify about the general Child Benefit rules before you contact them?

conversation.author: actor
conversation.text: No, I think that's all I needed to know for now. Thank you for your help - I'll get in touch with HMRC directly to discuss my situation. I appreciate you taking the time to explain things.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text: Based on our conversation, I need to provide an assessment of the eligibility situation for Alex.

conversation.author: eligibility_agent
conversation.text:
You're very welcome, and I wish you all the best with your inquiry. HMRC will be able to help you work through your specific circumstances confidentially and give you a definitive answer about your Child Benefit claim for Alex.

Take care!
